title: Best Electric Shavers UK
short: Foil and rotary electric shavers compared by closeness of shave, comfort and battery life, from budget picks to premium shaving systems.
intro: A shaver's price mostly buys motor power and how well the head adapts to your face, which matters most if you don't shave every single day. This guide compares shavers tested by Expert Reviews on day-old and three-day-old growth, judging shave quality, ergonomics, battery life and ease of cleaning.

products.name: Series 3 3040s
products.best_for: Budget buyers who want a reliable, no-frills foil shaver
products.key_spec: 3 floating foil elements, wet/dry use, 1hr charge for a week's shaving
products.summary: An affordable foil shaver with three independently floating elements that adapt to facial contours, usable in the shower and giving up to a week's shaving from a one-hour charge. Expert Reviews found shaving performance isn't up there with pricier models, needing a few passes for a close shave, and the power button can be brushed off accidentally.
pros: Usable wet or dry, including in the shower
cons: Needs a few passes for a close shave
Sensitive power button can switch off mid-shave

products.name: R6 Style Series Aqua
products.best_for: Buyers who want a waterproof rotary shaver with strong battery life
products.key_spec: Rotary, wet/dry, 60-minute battery, USB charging, 5-minute quick charge
products.summary: A well-specced budget rotary shaver that's fully waterproof for use with gel, foam or in the shower, with USB charging and a 5-minute quick-charge option. Expert Reviews found it comfortable for regular shaving with Twintrack blades handling thick jawline growth well, though it doesn't get quite as close as premium shavers and can tug on longer hairs.
pros: Excellent battery life for the price
Fully waterproof for wet or dry use
cons: Not as close a shave as premium models
products.search: Remington R6 Style Series Aqua shaver

products.name: Style Master
products.best_for: Buyers who want to maintain stubble rather than a clean shave
products.summary: Gillette's take on the OneBlade format, brilliant at trimming stubble on the neck, cheeks and jawline and maintaining a consistent two-to-three-day look, according to Expert Reviews. Blades stay sharp for months and it's fully waterproof, though it can't match a conventional shaver for a smooth, clean-cut finish.
pros: Excellent for trimming and maintaining stubble
cons: Can't give as close a shave as conventional shavers

products.name: F6 Style Series Aqua
products.badge: Best for use in the shower
products.best_for: Buyers who want premium features on a budget
products.key_spec: 2 independent flexing foils, intercept trimmer, USB charging
products.summary: Has the feel and features of pricier shavers at an affordable price, with a close shave for the money and a non-slip grip that's great when used wet. Expert Reviews found solid build quality bar a slightly flimsy pop-up trimmer, plus a handy 5-minute emergency charge and USB charging from any power bank or laptop.
pros: Premium features at an affordable price
USB charging, no dedicated charger needed
cons: Clip-on stubble styler is uncomfortable and ineffective

products.name: Shaver Series 5000
products.best_for: Buyers who want SkinIQ technology without a high-end price
products.key_spec: SkinIQ hair-density sensing, multi-directional pivoting heads, wet/dry
products.summary: Packs in SkinIQ technology from Philips' high-end range, sensing facial hair density and adapting motor power for an optimal shave. Expert Reviews found the heads pivot well for tricky areas, though a couple of tight spots around the jawline still needed extra passes, likely due to a larger-than-average head assembly.
pros: Close shaves at an affordable price
SkinIQ adapts power to hair density

products.name: Series 7 70-N7200cc
products.best_for: Buyers who want near-flagship performance without the flagship price
products.key_spec: 3 flexible blades, 360° Flex adaptive head, AutoSense power control, SmartCare Centre
products.summary: An even better successor to a shaver that already set a high standard, with a 360° Flex head that twists and pivots to follow facial contours and AutoSense technology that ramps power up for thicker stubble. Expert Reviews found it genuinely great at pushing through unruly growth with less of the 'plucking' feeling associated with electric shavers.
pros: Genuinely handles thick, unruly stubble well
Includes SmartCare cleaning and charging station
cons: Not for those on a tight budget
SmartCare Centre's indicator lights can be a little bright

products.name: Shaver Series 7000
products.best_for: Buyers who want app-based shaving feedback
products.key_spec: Self-sharpening SteelPrecision blades, Bluetooth GroomTribe app, cleaning pod compatible
products.summary: Gives most of the Series 9000's core technology at half the price, with redesigned heads that channel facial hair into the ideal cutting position. Expert Reviews liked the Bluetooth-connected GroomTribe app, which uses motion sensors to help track and improve shaving technique, though a supremely close shave still favours the pricier Series 9000.
pros: Most of the flagship technology at half the price
Bluetooth app tracks and helps improve technique
Works dry, with foam or gel, or in the shower
cons: Not the very closest shave available

products.name: ES-LV9Q
products.badge: Best shaving system for daily shaves
products.best_for: Buyers who shave every day and want the closest possible result
products.key_spec: 5-blade system, 70,000 cutting actions per minute, beard-density sensor
products.summary: A high-tech shaver Expert Reviews called incredibly close and 'frankly flawless' when used daily, with a pivoting head and beard-density sensor that boosts power where needed. It works best with a daily shaving routine, since longer hairs from a few days' growth can trip up the system, and its cleaning station is noisy.
pros: Incredibly close, flawless shave with daily use
Pivoting head adapts to facial contours
cons: Works best only if you shave daily

guide.a: Foil shavers generally suit those with sensitive skin, since the thin, straight blades under a foil guard are gentler and better for a daily shaving routine. Rotary shavers, with three spinning heads, tend to handle longer or less regularly trimmed facial hair and different growth directions better.

guide.q: How much difference does price actually make?
guide.a: Spending more generally buys a more powerful motor, a head that better adapts to your face's contours, and smarter sensing of beard density, all of which matter most if you don't shave every day. For a daily, close-cropped routine, a mid-range shaver like the Braun Series 7 here already delivers excellent results without flagship pricing.

guide.q: Do I need a cleaning station?
guide.a: A cleaning and charging station, like those bundled with the Braun Series 7 and 9, automatically cleans, lubricates and dries the shaver head, which extends its life and keeps performance consistent. It's a genuine convenience rather than a necessity, and most shavers can be rinsed under a tap instead if you don't mind doing it manually.

guide.q: Is a wet/dry shaver worth it?
guide.a: A wet/dry, fully waterproof shaver lets you shave in the shower with gel or foam, which many find more comfortable, and makes cleaning under a tap straightforward. Nearly every shaver in this guide supports both, so it's rarely worth paying extra to specifically seek it out.
